questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go to place that was very different and where I had never been. A place where I feel like I would learn a lot.

Secondly, I picked a destination with relevance to my academic interests.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, I would say. I was paired with a contact person from the host university, but did not end up needing him a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was paired with a local student and there was a bunch of introductory activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. I found one on Facebook before leaving and it only took me a couple of days. I know there are also a couple of local apps but I cant remember the name of any of them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's more expensive but living conditions are a lot nicer. Also, you don't see your friends all the time. Then a gain you get the chance to meet other people as you will likely have room mates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know if this question is referring to student housing? I did not live in the student dormitories but I was very happy with the housing I found by myself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to do a health check - however it was also possible to do it from home. Apart from that, you only had to bring all your papers and take part in the introductory activities.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: For the registration? As mentioned I had a contact person and there was also other people at the registration events.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I failed to gain a spot in one class but overall I would say I was very successful. I know others had a harder time, though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is pretty easy to drop and add classes so don't worry too much about taking classes you might not like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different between professors. I would say that overall the style of teaching was much more just open discussions (however, I think that only applies for graduate classes). No power point or a set agenda.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Political economy of China
Cross strait relations between China and Taiwan
Asian regionalism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of them. They were very interesting, the level was high, and the professors were good. 

Also, to do the optional Chinese classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing memorable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is cheaper than in Denmark but it's not like living in Vietnam or Indonesia. Especially food is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was A LOT of opportunities but I didn't actually end up taking a part in a lot of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I think that would be too many to list here (and definitely too many for me to look up).
https://osa_activity.ntu.edu.tw/en/club/list/type/0
This is an incomplete list.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There's a bunch of activities for exchange students but I would recommend also joining some local clubs. This is a good opportunity to get to know local people and they are very friendly towards foreigners.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Islands. Take the High speed rail down south. Go hiking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not have any big problems but of course the customs are very different. However, I would say that you mostly end up hanging out with the other exchange students anyways.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club. Learn Chinese.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Locals can be a bit shy and seem cold until you approach them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly towards foreigners.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't have too many expectations about how the semester is supposed to be. It won't be like that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every other exchange student is in the exact same position as you and all local students think you are pretty interesting. Don't be afraid to engage.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining now friends, new academic experiences and perspectives on issues, learning a new language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
